a:r.a:t: The biggest lesson from this project was that turning a model into a reliable deployed system takes more work than training the model itself.

Some challenges were deployment-related. Cloud Run required the API and UI to be configured as separate services, and Streamlit needed the correct MODEL_API_URL environment variable so it could call the public API endpoint. SARIMA also required extra care because the original artifact was too large and the API needed enough memory.

AI assistance was useful for scaffolding and troubleshooting. It helped with the Flask and Streamlit structure, Docker commands, deployment checks, and debugging. But I still had to manually verify the code, simplify generated pieces, check logs, run tests, and make sure the final project matched the course requirements.

For future work, I would add a scheduled EIA refresh so the deployed model can update automatically, add confidence intervals, include a feature importance or SHAP view, and continue reducing dependencies so Cloud Run rebuilds are faster.

Overall, this project gave me practice across the full data science workflow: data collection, preprocessing, model comparison, API design, frontend interaction, deployment, and presentation of results.
